observations.finding: All eight candidate sets (K8_C0001 through K8_C0008) screen at candidate_k=1, indicating the dominant gap is at the single-cluster resolution and no dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal is detected by this screen.

observations.meaning: Magnitude of the leading spectral eigengap at the screened resolution for each candidate set.

observations.meaning: Full eigengap profile across candidate resolutions for each set, showing the location and magnitude of the dominant gap.

observations.meaning: Average fused affinity among patients assigned to the same candidate set.
observations.finding: Within-set mean affinities are uniformly low and tightly ranged (approximately 0.0097–0.0104) across all sets, indicating weak internal fused-graph cohesion at this scale.

observations.meaning: Relatively close candidate pairs and their between-set fused affinity; a pair-review entry point, not a merge conclusion.

observations.finding: Set sizes range from 7 to 20 patients, so all structural measurements rest on small-to-moderate samples and should be read with corresponding uncertainty.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen addresses whether any current candidate shows an obvious internal subdivision signal and which candidate boundaries are relatively close in the fused patient geometry. Within-set mean affinities are uniformly low (~0.0097–0.0104), and the nearest between-set affinities (~0.0091–0.0093) are only slightly lower, so the fused geometry shows weak separation overall. The nearest-pair list is a pair-review entry point only and does not constitute a merge conclusion. No feasible k>=2 internal solutions are reported at this partition scope, so no finer-granularity subdivision is supported by these measurements. This evidence is triage-level and does not by itself establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not determine retention, split, or merge.
